text:
B: Hiya! Oh, there you are. Kirsty, is it?
A: Yeah. Hi.
B: I'm Gemma. Sorry if I look a state, I've just done three long days back to back, so I'm running on tea and biscuits.
A: Oh, no. You look fine. What do you do?
B: I'm a nurse, on a surgical ward in Taunton. It's good, mostly, but the twelve-hour shifts do knock you about a bit. What about you?
A: Erm, I'm not working at the minute. I was in a factory, but I got made redundant. I'm looking, though.
B: Oh, that's hard. Fingers crossed something comes up soon, yeah.
A: Thanks. Erm, Taunton, is that near the sea?
B: Sort of? Half an hour or so. We've got the Quantocks right there, though, which I love. I go walking up there with my friends when I'm off. It's lush on a clear day, you can see right over to Wales.
A: Oh, I walk a lot. Up by Pendle Hill mainly, near me.
B: Pendle, is that the witches one? I'm sure I've heard of it on a podcast.
A: Yeah. The Pendle witches. Sixteen-twelve.
B: I listen to so much true crime on the drive in, I swear I've heard an episode about it. Was it a whole family or something?
A: Erm, two families, sort of. The Demdikes and the Chattoxes. They'd been feuding for years, and then a girl called Alizon Device cursed a pedlar who wouldn't give her some pins, and he collapsed, probably a stroke, and it all came out from there. And the main witness was her little sister, Jennet, she was only nine, and she stood up in court in Lancaster and accused her own mum. And they hanged ten of them. What gets me is they were just poor, really, begging and that, and people were scared of them. Sorry, I'm going on.
B: No, don't be sorry, that's fascinating! A nine-year-old? That's proper grim.
A: It is. You can walk the route they took to Lancaster now. There's a trail.
B: Oh, I'd do that. Have you done it?
A: Bits of it. I'd like to do all of it one day. I'd need to plan it, though, with the buses.
B: I'm the opposite, I just turn up and hope. My partner Liam gets so annoyed with me.
A: I'd be terrified doing that.
B: It goes wrong sometimes, to be fair. We went camping in Pembrokeshire and I hadn't booked anywhere, and we ended up in a farmer's field with about forty cows. Erm, I saw a cat in your photo?
A: Yeah, Moss. She's asleep on the settee right now, actually. She's sixteen.
B: Aw, bless her. Sixteen's a good age. We haven't got pets, Liam's allergic, or he says he is.
A: Says he is?
B: I've seen him stroke my mum's dog for ten minutes and not sneeze once. I'm keeping a file.
A: You should give it me, I'll be a witness.
B: Ha! You're on. Do you draw as well? There was a picture on the wall behind you.
A: Yeah. That's the canal lock near me. I do bits, it's just pencil.
B: Just pencil, she says. It looked really good on the little photo. I can't draw a cat without it looking like a potato.
A: Everyone's cats look like potatoes at first. Mine did.
B: That's actually really reassuring. Oh, hang on, is that the—
